scoring_justification: Agent-submitted CSVs are the raw artifacts; checker recomputes physical trends (C_V T³ dependence, Dulong-Petit approach, pressure monotonicity, monotonic σ/τ) and compares specific values to paper-reported gold with appropriate tolerances.

outputs.description: Computed constant-volume heat capacity, thermal expansion coefficient, and Grüneisen parameter at specified temperatures and pressures.
Computed Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity (per relaxation time), total thermal conductivity, and power factor at specified temperatures.

output_contract.notes: The checker will recompute target metrics from the submitted CSV rows (e.g., C_V at 370 K, α at 300 K, γ at 300 K, Seebeck at 300 K, κ at 300 K, PF at 300 K, and trends) and compare them to hidden paper-derived reference values using appropriate tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Inline gold values for thermodynamic and transport properties at selected (T,P) points; Dulong-Petit reference constant.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper reported values (J. Electron. Mater. 2018 Fig.3-9) and the classical Dulong-Petit limit for 17 atoms (3*17*R = 423.99 J/mol·K). Transport gold derived from paper text: Seebeck ≈ -158 µV/K, κ ≈ 1.8 W/mK, PF ≈ 2.13×10¹⁴ µW/(cm·K²·s) at 300 K.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's explicit numeric statements and confirmed against the reference solve.sh oracle rows.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values directly trace to the published paper; no random fabrication.

steps.description: Validate format, recompute key thermodynamic quantities (C_V Dulong-Petit, T³ law, alpha, gamma, pressure trends) and compare to paper gold.
Validate format, recompute transport trends (Seebeck, kappa, PF, sigma monotonic) and compare to paper gold at 300 K.
